title: Which months do I plant or move a rose?

common.applies_to: Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora bush rose in New Zealand, Australia, the United Kingdom or the United States; answer to a common question
common.preserved_uncertainty: New Zealand: Named planting months come from one company nationally and from one organisation for Canterbury. Auckland Botanic Gardens says autumn or winter, of container plants (C-8). All sources on moving are commercial, and one garden centre gives two different answers on its own pages (C-7). The potted-rose statement rests on two companies. Australia: The edges of the bare-root window differ: from May in two sources, and into August in South Australia (C-6). The Canberra page that named August could not be opened (AF-32). That potted roses can be planted at any time is one Sydney garden centre's statement (AF-64). Only the Victorian society names a month for moving a rose, and it does not say winter or dormant. Named months for New South Wales, Victoria and Western Australia each rest on one society. United Kingdom: The whole bare-root range, October to early March, is on one garden company's page; the RHS names seasons only and leaves out the middle of winter, while one rose grower calls December one of the best months (C-4). Months for moving a rose differ (C-5), and the RHS window is for deciduous shrubs in general, not roses. The ideal months for potted roses, and the warning about extreme heat, each rest on one source. United States: Every planting and moving month rests on one organisation in its own place. Places differ on the season for moving a rose, from fall (Illinois) to December to March (Arizona's low desert, Nashville, Arkansas, Marin County) and early spring (Iowa); the Nashville society's own pages give two times. Florida's months say when bare-root roses are on sale, not when to plant them. Missouri's -10 °F line for bare-root planting is already in Pip's US answer on planting (PKR-CGD-000016) and is on record only here (AF-99).

content.heading: Which months do I plant or move a rose?

items.text: In New Zealand, winter is the best time to plant a rose, and planting can go on through spring. One garden company says June and July are the best months. Months are only a guide.
New roses for winter planting reach garden centres from June. Months are only a guide.

In Canterbury, one source says to plant roses in June, July and August, while they are dormant. July and August are its months for bare-root roses, which are sold without soil on their roots. Months are only a guide.
In Auckland, one source says roses are best planted in autumn or winter.
A rose in a pot can be planted at any time of year. Keep it well watered if you plant in spring or summer.
Move an established rose in winter, while it is dormant. One garden centre page says autumn instead.

For moving a rose, one garden centre says July, after pruning and once the risk of frost has passed. One garden company says June or July. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.
In Australia, plant a bare-root rose (a dormant plant sold in winter, with no leaves or flowers) in June or July. One source says planting can start in May. Months are only a guide.
Move an established rose in winter, while it is dormant.
Don't plant a rose in very hot weather.
In New South Wales, one rose society says to prepare the soil in late April or May, for planting in June or July. Months are only a guide.
In Sydney, one garden centre says a rose in a pot can be planted at any time of year, though not in very hot weather.
In Victoria, one rose society says to order new roses in May and start planting them in June. It also says to move an established rose in June. Months are only a guide.
In South Australia, plant a bare-root rose in June or July. Planting can go on into August. Months are only a guide.
In Western Australia, one rose society says to plant new roses in May, and to plant or repot as needed in June and July. Months are only a guide.
In the UK, plant a bare-root rose (one sold without soil on its roots) while it is dormant (not actively growing), between October and early March. Months are only a guide.
Don't plant a bare-root rose while the ground is frozen. One rose grower says to keep it in a bucket of water or compost until the ground has thawed.

A rose in a pot can be planted at any time of year, as long as the ground is not frozen, waterlogged or very dry. One garden company says the ideal months are September to November and March to May. Months are only a guide.
One rose grower says not to plant a potted rose in extreme heat.

Move an established rose while it is dormant, between November and February. One source says shrubs that drop their leaves in winter can be moved at any time from late October to mid-March. Months are only a guide.
A rose in a pot can be planted at almost any time during the growing season.

In Iowa, one extension service says to plant a bare-root rose (one sold while dormant, not actively growing) in early spring, before growth begins, as soon as you get it: in late March or April. It says a rose in a pot can go in from April through midsummer. Months are only a guide.
In Iowa, one extension service says to move an established rose in early spring, before it leafs out, usually late March to mid-April. Months are only a guide.

In Minnesota, one rose society says to plant bare-root roses (sold while dormant, not actively growing) between April 10 and May 15, and roses in pots from May 15 on through the growing season. One rose expert says to plant a bare-root rose as soon as the soil can be worked. Months are only a guide.
In Wisconsin, one rose expert says to plant a bare-root rose (one sold while dormant, not actively growing) as soon as the soil can be worked and plants are available.
In Illinois, one extension service says fall is a good time to move a rose.

In Colorado, one extension service says to plant a bare-root rose (one sold while dormant, not actively growing) in spring rather than fall, and to finish by mid-April at the lower elevations of the state. Months are only a guide.
In Colorado, one extension service says a rose in a pot can be planted during the growing season, any time after the last killing frost.
In the Kansas City area, one extension source says to plant roses grown in containers after May 1. Months are only a guide.

In Nashville, one rose society says to plant a bare-root rose (one sold while dormant, not actively growing) in March. It says to move an established rose while it is dormant or going dormant, ideally from December to the first of February. Months are only a guide.
In Arkansas, one extension service says the dormant season, between November and February, is the best time to move a rose. Months are only a guide.

In South Carolina, one extension service says to plant bare-root roses (sold while dormant, not actively growing) in late fall, late winter or early spring, and roses grown in containers later in spring.

In Florida, one extension service says bare-root roses (sold while dormant, not actively growing) are usually on sale from October to March, and that roses can be planted all year round, except in North Florida, where early spring is better. Months are only a guide.

In Arizona's low desert, one extension service says the best time to plant a bare-root rose (one sold while dormant, not actively growing) is mid-December through February. It says a rose in a pot can be planted at any time of year, but spring or fall is best. Months are only a guide.
In Arizona's low desert, one extension service says the best time to move a rose is from December through March. Months are only a guide.

In Marin County, one rose society says bare-root roses (sold while dormant, not actively growing) reach nurseries in December, and to plant them in January and finish in February. It says December, along with pruning, is also a good time to move a rose. Months are only a guide.
In Orange County, California, one rose society says January is the season for bare-root roses (sold while dormant, not actively growing). Months are only a guide.
